question.text: For a Semiconductor use case involving RFIC validation, where would Oscilloscope fit in the test workflow?

messages.text: For a Semiconductor use case involving RFIC validation, where would Oscilloscope fit in the test workflow?

In the RFIC validation workflow, the oscilloscope fits **beside—not instead of—the RF signal generation/analysis chain**: RF signal generators/VSGs provide the RF stimulus, RF analyzers/VSA/VSE handle RF analysis, and the oscilloscope is used for time-domain electrical validation around the DUT, test board, measurement path, PDN, ADC/DAC frontend, reference clock/PLL jitter, and interface behavior [7][14].  
R&S’s O-RU testing context explicitly separates these roles: R&S provides RF signal generation and signal analysis interfaces to the tester [13], and the broader R&S equipment set can include RF signal generation, signal analysis, VSE, power supply, oscilloscope, RF switch/OSP, or standalone VSA/VSG equipment [14].  
What the oscilloscope measures in this workflow is the **time-domain electrical behavior** needed for validation, such as signal-integrity items including eye diagram and TDR impedance, and validation areas such as power distribution network behavior, ADC/DAC frontend performance, reference clock and PLL jitter performance, and interface tests [7][8][9].  
【推論】For Semiconductor RFIC validation, use the oscilloscope to observe the DUT/test-board electrical and timing-domain behavior while the VSG/VSA or RF signal generation/analysis instruments handle the RF stimulus and RF measurement path [7][13][14].
